feedback.answered: Completed representative recovery, membership and Node completion trace. ConfState restoration retains AutoLeave; Node permits messages while awaiting Advance; only nonempty apply responses or snapshot completion call raft.appliedTo. Transfer abort clears only its target. The automatic-exit interface supplies implementation ownership, but no numeric exit deadline. Existing leadership-loss test has a new-leader application trigger and does not answer the same-leader abort question. Retained pending reads are released with a fresh committed index and safe-read acknowledgements, so queue retention alone is not evidence of stale authority reuse.
remaining: Construct and execute the legal automatic-exit/transfer overlap; account for all pending completions and post-abort continuation.
Independent switchToConfig pending-read release premise remains a mapped surface.
feedback.rationale: Turns earlier broad unknowns into sourced conditional relationships and selects the narrow remaining continuation discriminator without alleging a violation.

question.question: After an implicit joint configuration is committed and applied by a leader, can rejection of its automatic exit proposal during leadership transfer consume the last application trigger, leaving no implementation-owned retry when that transfer aborts and the same leader remains healthy?
question.importance: A lost automatic-exit continuation can retain outgoing voter requirements and block later configuration changes despite an available quorum; no consensus-safety violation is currently alleged.
contexts: No unrelated client proposals after configuration application
event_paths: Commit implicit joint entry -> initiate transfer -> apply configuration and complete application while transfer active -> automatic proposal rejected -> transfer timeout abort -> continue ordinary ticks and transport

question.trigger_rationale: Source narrows retry to real appliedTo calls while transfer timeout only clears a field. This is a specific missing-continuation premise. Contract reading supplies library ownership; a small serialized multi-node execution can now distinguish hidden pending completion from a lost trigger. It is more direct than the separate pending-read/configuration history question.
